title: 2D Shapes & Symmetry
description: Class 4 Maths: 2D shapes and polygons (triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon), their sides and corners, and lines of symmetry — with worked examples and tests.

topics.title: Polygons — Sides & Corners
topics.concept:
A polygon is a closed shape made of straight sides. We name polygons by their number of sides:

Triangle3 sides
Quadrilateral4 sides (square, rectangle…)
Pentagon5 sides
Hexagon6 sides

A polygon has the same number of corners (vertices) as sides.

topics.title: Lines of Symmetry
topics.concept:
A shape has a line of symmetry if you can fold it so the two halves match exactly. Some shapes have more than one line of symmetry.

  • A square has 4 lines of symmetry.
  • A rectangle has 2.
  • A circle has endless lines of symmetry.
  • A scalene triangle has none.

examples.problem: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
Does the letter A have a line of symmetry?
examples.solution: Yes — a vertical line down the middle. 1 line.

recap: A line of symmetry folds a shape into two matching halves.
Square 4, rectangle 2, circle endless, scalene triangle 0.
Some shapes have more than one line of symmetry.
